candidates.statement: Gateway checkout returns 502 because its downstream call to order returns HTTP 500. Traces and logs show POST /v1/orders failing with 500 (HTTPStatusError) on the order service, propagating as 502 on /v1/checkout across all correlated requests.
candidates.uncertainty: Order-side root cause (db, payment, inventory) not observed; only gateway-side evidence available.

report.explanation: Gateway 502s on /v1/checkout are consistently caused by the order service returning HTTP 500 on POST /v1/orders, as shown in correlated traces and client-request warn logs. The bounded candidate is http-500 at the order dependency; the deeper order-internal cause is not yet observed.
missing_evidence: Order service logs/traces showing the internal cause of its 500 responses
Order dependency metrics (postgresql, payment, inventory) to rule out db-pool-exhaustion or downstream-latency
